column1: To see whether the evidence supports this conclusion, we again look at cross-country data. Figure 8-13 is a scatterplot of data for the same countries examined in the previous Case Study (and in Figure 8-6). The figure shows that countries with high rates of population growth tend to have low levels of income per person. The international evidence is consistent with our model’s prediction that the rate of population growth is one determinant of a country’s standard of living.
